title: Reassessment of pre-industrial fire emissions strongly affects anthropogenic aerosol forcing
problem: Existing climate models underestimate pre-industrial fire emissions by incorrectly assuming fire activity increases with population, which leads to a significant overestimation of the historical radiative forcing from anthropogenic aerosols and thus uncertainty in climate projections.
method: The paper uses two global fire models to simulate revised pre-industrial fire emissions and implements them in a global aerosol model to reassess historical aerosol concentrations and the magnitude of anthropogenic radiative forcing compared to standard estimates.
task: The task is to reassess pre-industrial fire emissions using global models, showing that previously underestimated emissions led to a significant overestimation of historical anthropogenic aerosol radiative forcing and were the largest source of uncertainty in pre-industrial aerosol concentrations.
